title: Stratifying Colorectal Cancer Patients by Gut Enterovirus Abundance
text: Following bootstrap calculations, OptSurvCutR evaluates Precision (Confidence Interval width relative overall data range) Validity (absence interval overlap), grading model health four distinct tiers: Tier 1 (OPTIMAL): Narrow intervals (CI Width < 30%) paired complete cohort separation. Tier 2 (DISTINCT): Zero overlap confidence zones regardless width. Thresholds may float slightly, risk boundaries remain clear. Tier 3 (CAUTION): Moderate parameter variance (CI Width 30%–60%) accompanied overlapping intervals. Tier 4 (UNSTABLE): High variance (CI Width > 60%) overlapping intervals, signaling severe data -fitting. what: 4.1 Engineering Solutions: Deploying the nmin Wedge
title: Stratifying Colorectal Cancer Patients by Gut Enterovirus Abundance
text: Biomarker distributions human clinical populations rarely match flawless, neat step-functions. cross-validation 3-tier risk architecture, may occasionally run overlapping confidence intervals Cut 1 Cut 2. Overlap Problem: early baseline tuning passes raw dataset, setting standard nmin = 0.25 caused algorithm place Cut 1 Cut 2 close together. subjected bootstrap resampling, 95% confidence intervals bled heavily (e.g., Cut 1 upper bound reaching 1.89, Cut 2 lower bound dropped 1.77). overlapping variance triggered automated Tier 4 (UNSTABLE) flag , certain resampled cohorts, intermediate group vanished entirely, causing underlying Cox calculations collapse. Solution: resolved without changing core clinical objective slightly increasing minimum group size constraint nmin = 0.275. mandating every individual cohort must hold least 27.5% total sample size, effectively injected mathematical “wedge” search space. parameter physically forces Cut 1 Cut 2 apart accommodate minimum required patient volume . demonstrated final Tier 1 output , confidence intervals now separate cleanly, yielding highly stable reproducible clinical tiers.

title: Optimal Survival Cut-Point Discovery for Time-to-Event Analysis
code: library(OptSurvCutR) library(survival) library(dplyr)  data("crc_virome")  # Quick data preparation crc <- crc_virome %>%   mutate(event = as.numeric(substr(status, 1, 1))) %>%    select(time = time_months, event, abundance = Enterovirus) %>%   filter(complete.cases(.))  # Step 1: Determine the optimal number of cut-points num_res <- find_cutpoint_number(   data = crc, predictor = "abundance",   outcome_time = "time", outcome_event = "event",   method = "genetic", criterion = "BIC",   max_cuts = 3, nmin = 0.25, seed = 123 ) summary(num_res)  # Step 2: Find the precise cut-point locations cut_res <- find_cutpoint(   data = crc, predictor = "abundance",   outcome_time = "time", outcome_event = "event",   method = "genetic", criterion = "logrank",   num_cuts = num_res$optimal_num_cuts,  # Dynamically pass the result from Step 1   nmin = 0.275,                         # Fine-tuned for stability   n_perm = 50, n_cores = 2, seed = 123 ) summary(cut_res)  # Automatically reports Hazard Ratios & Schoenfeld Diagnostics!  # Step 3: Validate stability with bootstrap val_res <- validate_cutpoint(   cutpoint_result = cut_res,   num_replicates = 150, n_cores = 2, seed = 123 ) summary(val_res)  # Automatically grades threshold stability (Tiers 1-4)!  # Step 4: Visualise outcomes via atomic native plots plot(cut_res, type = "distribution")   # Continuous Predictor Density Split Map plot(cut_res, type = "outcome")        # Premium Custom Kaplan-Meier Survival Curves plot(cut_res, type = "forest")         # Hazard Ratio Forest Plot with Cohort Sample Sizes plot(cut_res, type = "diagnostic")     # Schoenfeld Residual Proportional Hazards Check plot_validation(val_res, focus_cuts = c(1, 2)) # 2D Contour Elevation Stability Topology
